chunks: From him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahbub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about the saying of Allah, Exalted and Mighty: 'And whoever enters it is safe,' whether he meant the House or the Sanctuary.
He said: 'Whoever enters the Sanctuary from among people seeking refuge in it, he is safe from the wrath of Allah,
and whoever enters it from among beasts and birds is safe from being attacked or harmed until he exits the Sanctuary.'

key_terms.الْحَرَمَ: The Sanctuary (specifically Mecca or general sacred precincts)

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of safety for humans and animals in the Islamic Sanctuary according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the scope of 'safety' (aman) in the Sanctuary by distinguishing between spiritual and physical protection. He clarifies that for humans seeking refuge, safety denotes deliverance from Allah's wrath, whereas for wild beasts and birds, it signifies protection from being attacked or harmed while within the sacred boundaries.
